'''Alessandro De Angelis''' (born 16 August 1959 in [[Cencenighe Agordino]], Italy) is an Italian and [[Argentina|Argentine]] physicist and astrophysicist. A professor of Experimental Physics at the [[University of Padova]]<ref name=a/> and Professor Catedratico of Astroparticle Physics at [[Instituto Superior Técnico|IST Lisboa]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fenix.tecnico.ulisboa.pt/departamentos/df/docentes|title=Docentes Fisica Lisboa}}</ref> he is mostly known for his role in the proposal, construction and data analysis of new telescopes for gamma-ray astrophysics. He is a member of  [[INFN|Istituto nazionale di fisica nucleare]] (INFN), [[INAF|Istituto nazionale di astrofisica]] (INAF), [[Italian Physical Society]] (SIF), [[International Astronomical Union]] (IAU),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iau.org/administration/membership/individual/19901/|title=IAU Members: Alessandro De Angelis|access-date=2021-05-14|archive-date=2022-03-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220302161620/https://www.iau.org/administration/membership/individual/19901/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Gruppo2003.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gruppo2003.org/|title=Per una rinascita della ricerca scientifica in Italia|access-date=3 November 2020}}</ref>

== Career ==
De Angelis graduated in physics from the [[University of Padova]] in 1983 studying charmed particles produced in the [[LExan Bubble Chamber]] at the [[European Hybrid Spectrometer]]. Had a post-doctoral activity at [[CERN]] ending as a staff member in [[Ugo Amaldi (physicist)|Ugo Amaldi]]'s [[DELPHI experiment]].
Back to Italy, since 1999 he works mostly to particle astrophysics. He participated to the design and construction of [[NASA]]'s [[Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope]] and of the [[MAGIC (telescope)|MAGIC Telescopes]] in the Canary Island of [[La Palma]]. He is principal investigator of the space project [[e-ASTROGAM|ASTROGAM]]<ref name=a /> and is among the proponents of the Southern Wide-field Gamma-ray Observatory ([[SWGO]]), a very-high-energy gamma-rays observatory to be constructed on the [[Andes]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sif.it/riviste/sif/ncc/econtents/2017/040/03/article/8|title=LATTES: A new gamma-ray detector concept for South America}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.swgo.org|title=The Southern Wide-field Gamma-ray Observatory (SWGO)}}</ref> He proposed the mixing between gamma rays and axions in intergalactic magnetic fields.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.76.121301|title=Evidence for a new light spin-zero boson from cosmological gamma-ray propagation?|journal=Physical Review D |date=18 December 2007 |volume=76 |issue=12 |article-number=121301 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.76.121301 |last1=De Angelis |first1=Alessandro |last2=Roncadelli |first2=Marco |last3=Mansutti |first3=Oriana |arxiv=0707.4312 |bibcode=2007PhRvD..76l1301D|s2cid=119152884 }}</ref>

From 2010 to 2011 he has been guest scientist at the [[Max Planck Institute for Physics|Werner Heisenberg Max Planck Institute for Physics]] in Munich, and since 2014 has been for three years Director of Research at [[INFN]].<ref name=a />

He also works on popularization of science and on history and philosophy of physics, in particular in relation to cosmic rays<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ilnuovosaggiatore.sif.it/article/198|title=Cosmic rays, Il Nuovo Saggiatore, Settembre 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lescienze.it/archivio/articoli/2012/08/01/news/gli_enigmi_dei_raggi_cosmici-1172332/|title=Alessandro De Angelis, Gli enigmi dei raggi cosmici, Le Scienze, Agosto 2012|date=25 July 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fisica.uniud.it/MAGIC/documents/MagicSciAm.pdf|title=Alessandro De Angelis e Luigi Peruzzo, Le magie del telescopio MAGIC, Le Scienze, Marzo 2007}}</ref> and to the Galilei period.<ref>{{Citation|last = Alessandro De Angelis and Catarina Espirito Santo|year = 2015|title = The contribution of Giordano Bruno to the principle of relativity|url = http://www.narit.or.th/en/files/2015JAHHvol18/2015JAHH...18..241D.pdf|journal = Journal of Astronomical History and Heritage|volume = 18|issue = 3|pages = 241√ź248| doi=10.3724/SP.J.1440-2807.2015.03.02 |arxiv = 1504.01604|bibcode = 2015JAHH...18..241D|access-date = 2021-05-14|archive-date = 2016-01-26|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160126194011/http://www.narit.or.th/en/files/2015JAHHvol18/2015JAHH...18..241D.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|publisher= Codice
|language= it

|first= Alessandro

|location= Torino

== Prizes ==
* Highly Cited Researcher, Thomson-Reuters/Clarivate, 2016<ref name=a/>
* Thomson-Reuters Award for belonging to the "top 1% researchers publishing in the field of Space Science over the [...] decade" 2001–2010, 2011<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/inter/aut/2011/11-nov/11-novDeAn/|title=ALESSANDRO DE ANGELIS ON HIGH-ENERGY GAMMY RAY ASTRONOMY}}</ref>
* [[American Astronomical Society]]'s [[Bruno Rossi Prize]] with the Fermi LAT Team, 2011<ref name=a>{{cite web|url=https://persone.csia.unipd.it/persone/curriculum/C88026E218E1EB5C32194C4BA39899D9.pdf|title=Alessandro De Angelis CV|publisher=Universita di Padova|access-date=13 October 2020}}</ref>
* Highlight of the European Physical Society<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.europhysicsnews.org/vol-42-no-2-highlights|title=EPS Highights}}</ref> for the article "Nationalism and internationalism in science: the case of the discovery of cosmic rays", with P. Carlson, Eur. Phys. J. H 36, 309, 2010
* [[NASA Group Achievement Award]], 2008<ref name=a/>
